scenes.headline: How to read a viral model from its files
scenes.sub: A small hybrid-attention model, checked without running it
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Parfait! A small open model went viral with big claims. Let's read its files before running any of it.

scenes.text: A checkpoint is evidence you can read without running it. The config, the tensor headers and the loader code say what a model is before any benchmark does.
scenes.mark: evidence you can read without running it
scenes.say: A checkpoint is evidence. Its config, tensor headers and loader code say what the model is, before any benchmark does.

scenes.title: Three local layers, then one global

steps.say: Tokens become vectors from its own vocabulary.
Three layers only look back five hundred and twelve tokens.
Then one layer sees the whole context. Only its cache grows with the input.
The unit repeats nine times, thirty six layers in all.

steps.label: Sliding window
steps.say: A sliding layer sees a short band behind each token, so its memory stays fixed.

steps.label: Full attention
steps.say: A full layer sees everything before it. That is where long context costs memory.
The model card draws the same layout, repeated.
Its spec table gives a parameter count we can check against the files.

scenes.title: Checking the weights by range request

steps.say: Read a few kilobytes from each shard. The tensor shapes add up to the card's count exactly.
Then fetch one weight matrix from it and from likely bases, and compare rows.
Against its own base, a near perfect match. Against the others, only noise. These are its own weights.

parts.note: full layers, a key and a value
parts.say: Nine full layers store a key and a value per token.
Four heads of two hundred fifty six numbers, two bytes each.
About thirty seven thousand bytes for every token kept.

scenes.title: Cache at a million tokens
scenes.say: At a million tokens, thirty six gibibytes. The hybrid saves four times over, yet needs twice a laptop's memory.

scenes.text: The model is real and its own. The million tokens and the laptop are two different deployments.
scenes.say: The model is real and cleanly built. But the million tokens and the laptop are two different deployments.

recap: Read config, headers and code first
Match one tensor against likely bases
Price the context in cache bytes
scenes.say: Read the files first. Match a tensor. Price the context in bytes.
